sections.h2: Who handles property tax inside the Todd County courthouse?
sections.html:
Todd County puts its tax work in one building: the courthouse at 202 East Washington Street in Elkton. All three offices answer through the county switchboard at (270) 265-9966, each on its own extension.

  • Sheriff, ext. 208: takes payment of property tax bills. The sheriff's website lets owners view their bills online and says payment cannot be made there, so ask the office which payment methods it accepts.
  • Property Valuation Administration (PVA), ext. 504: the county's answer for the value of a property and for disputing that value.
  • County clerk, ext. 501: registers vehicles and, after April 15, runs the delinquent-tax process.

The City of Elkton keeps a separate property tax payment link on its own website. If your address is inside the city, ask the city whether a city bill exists in addition to the county bill.

sections.h2: What sets Todd County apart from the counties around it?
sections.html:
Todd County spans 377 square miles and almost none of it is water, 2.6 square miles in all. The legislature created it on April 1, 1820, from parts of Christian and Logan counties, after residents petitioned for a seat of government closer than the two existing ones. It was named for Colonel John Todd, killed at the Battle of Blue Licks in 1782.

Historically the county divides into a northern high country of steep sandstone slopes with oak, walnut and poplar, and a southern low country of rolling limestone flatlands. The lowlands, with Pembroke soil, are known for strong crop yields, and farming is a long-standing local tradition. In the early 1800s a stagecoach hub at what is now Guthrie sent routes out to larger cities. Elkton took its name from the elk that watered at a spring near the center of town, and its courthouse square was laid out as a trapezoid rather than a square, so buildings on both sides catch sunlight longer.

The cities are Elkton, Guthrie and Trenton, with Allensville and Fairview (mostly in Christian County) as census-designated places. Muhlenberg, Logan and Christian counties border Todd, as do Robertson and Montgomery counties in Tennessee. Todd County runs on Central time and has a single public school district, the Todd County School District, with Todd County Central High School.

sections.h2: What do the Census figures say about Todd County homes?
sections.html:
Todd County counted 12,972 residents in July 2025, up 5.9 percent from the 2020 base after a small slide during the 2010s. The housing figures matter most to a seller:

  • A typical owner-occupied home is worth $166,700, the lowest figure of the four counties in this comparison.
  • Owners live in 76.0 percent of homes, across 4,559 households.
  • Gross rent in the middle of the range is $851, above Taylor and Trigg.
  • 5,313 housing units stood in the county in 2025, and 40 building permits were issued.
  • Household income sits at $61,103, and the trip to work averages 27.8 minutes.

In 2020, 10.8 percent of housing units were vacant and 30.0 percent of occupied homes were rented. Retail sales for 2022 came to $150.3 million. Todd also has the youngest population of the four, with 27.2 percent of residents under 18 and 7.6 percent under 5.

sections.h2: How has Todd County's population moved over time?
sections.html:
The headcount peaked around the start of the twentieth century and has hovered near 12,000 for decades. The county has not grown steadily the way Spencer has.

sections.h2: When do Todd County property tax bills go delinquent?
sections.html:
The sheriff's file closes at the end of the day on April 15. Every bill still open then goes to the county clerk, a lien is recorded, and the bill takes the name certificate of delinquency. Before that date, the state's schedule decides the cost: a 2 percent reduction through November 1, the printed amount until year end, 5 percent more in January, then 10 percent plus the sheriff's add-on fee.

After transfer, interest of 1 percent a month runs, and clerk and attorney commissions follow. The Department of Revenue's sample shows a $1,000 bill reaching $1,254 on arrival at the clerk, costing $1,387.79 if paid within five business days, and costing a third-party purchaser $1,704.21 at the sale. Waiting adds money fast, and the attorney's commission is waived only during that first five-day window.

sections.h2: When does the Todd County tax sale happen?
sections.html:
Kentucky places the sale between 90 and 135 days after the clerk receives the bills, which on a regular schedule means July 14 through August 28. Each year the clerk lists the sequence in order: a half-page notice, the published list, the deadline for outside buyers to register, and the sale itself, which begins at 9 AM.

A buyer of up to three bills registers with the county, while anyone wanting more than three registers with the state. The clerk stresses that buying a bill does not make the purchaser the owner; it places a lien on the house, and the owner then pays the purchaser, who may add costs. Owners get two mailed notices from the county attorney before the sale, and the list appears in the newspaper 30 to 45 days ahead.

sections.h2: How do I dispute a Todd County assessment?
sections.html:
The county FAQ sends valuation questions to the PVA in the courthouse, extension 504. A conference there is mandatory. The appeal itself is filed with the clerk the workday after the May viewing period closes, and a panel of area property owners hears it a few weeks later, for as many as five days.

The panel wants evidence: nearby sales, an appraisal, construction costs or insurance records. If an owner does not file locally or skips the hearing, the Kentucky Claims Commission is off the table. Paid representatives must be professionals such as attorneys, accountants, brokers or appraisers and must hold written authorization.

sections.h2: What does the homestead exemption mean for a Todd County sale?
sections.html:
The exemption removes $49,100 of assessed value for 2025 and 2026 from a home owned and lived in by someone past 65 or totally disabled. The Todd County PVA takes applications through December 31. The benefit belongs to the owner and not the house, so a buyer files again.

For closing, ask the sheriff for a payoff and the clerk about any older certificate. Each year's bill is the January 1 owner's personal debt, and a delinquent lien can remain for up to eleven years, so a title agent will want a clean record before releasing funds.

faqs.q: Where is a Todd County property tax bill paid?
faqs.a: At the sheriff's office on the courthouse's ground floor at 202 East Washington Street, extension 208 of (270) 265-9966. The sheriff's website lets you view bills, and the office can tell you which payment methods it takes.

faqs.q: Who reviews a Todd County assessment I disagree with?
faqs.a: The PVA, at extension 504. Ask for a conference, since the local board will not hear an appeal from an owner who skipped that meeting.

faqs.q: What is the Todd County homestead deduction?
faqs.a: $49,100 through the 2026 tax period, for owners past 65 or totally disabled. File with the PVA before the end of the year.

faqs.q: Can an investor buy my delinquent Todd County bill?
faqs.a: Yes. After April 15 the bill sits at the clerk's office, and an outside purchaser can buy it at the yearly sale and then collect from you.

faqs.q: Can a Todd County house with unpaid tax be sold?
faqs.a: Yes, so long as the amount owed is paid from the sale. Get written payoffs from the sheriff and clerk so the buyer's closing agent sees no surprises.
